sections.h2: Which Screven County offices send and set the tax?
sections.html:
Every Screven bill passes through two desks. Valuation belongs to the Board of Tax Assessors. Billing, receipts and tag work belong to the elected commissioner, whose FAQ says the office also handles timber and mobile home accounts.

  • Tax Commissioner, 216 Mims Road #103, Sylvania, GA 30467. Phone 912-564-2206. Walk-in hours: weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Tax Assessors, 912-564-7918, for returns, value questions and homestead forms.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: the deed room in the courthouse holds your recorded deed.

The state revenue department's Screven fact sheet says some cities collect their own levy through a city clerk. The commissioner can tell you whether yours does.

sections.h2: How does Screven County's profile affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Screven is rural. Its 645.78 square miles hold about 22 people for each square mile, and the July 2025 estimate of 14,408 is 2.5 percent over the April 2020 base of 14,061. The tax office is in Sylvania.

The Census QuickFacts table counts 4,932 households and 6,640 housing units. Homes with a resident owner make up 69.8 percent. Median value of an owned home is $124,300, median monthly rent is $679 and median household income is $52,792. Persons 65 and over are 23.7 percent of the county, the highest share of the four places covered here. Poverty is 21.1 percent.

New construction is minimal, with 19 permits in 2025, and 89.1 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. A house left empty after a death or a move stands out in a county like this. Bills run small beside metro Georgia, yet an unpaid year stays with the parcel and keeps collecting interest.

sections.h2: When does Screven County, GA want its property tax?
sections.html:
The office posts two different dates, so follow the one printed on your own bill. One page puts real estate and business personal property due on November 15 from 2018 on. Another puts the deadline at December 20.

Late rules posted on the Screven County Tax Commissioner's website
Where postedDueCharges after the date
FAQ pageNovember 151 percent interest per month and a single 10 percent charge at day 90
General information pageDecember 20Monthly interest of prime plus 3 percent over 12, and 5 percent added every 120 days, to a ceiling of 20 percent
Mobile homesApril 110 percent penalty

The state fact sheet holds interest back for 60 days from the bill's postmark. Mailed checks are judged by the Postal Service postmark; metered stamps are refused. Phone the counter for a current balance.

sections.h2: What does a Screven County lien or levy look like?
sections.html:
Thirty days past due, the office may have a fi. fa. (a tax lien) entered with the superior court clerk. Bureaus pull from those records, and the commissioner says it cannot control their use of the entry.

The next stage hands the account to a contractor named DTSi. Administration and levy charges of $215.00 or more land on the bill, covering certified mail and a title search. The house is posted and photographed, and an ad runs for the four weeks ahead of a sale in a newspaper, the Sylvester Local, at the owner's expense.

Clear it before listing, because the buyer's title search will find it.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Screven County valuation?
sections.html:
Each January 1 the assessors fix a market value, and 40 percent of it is taxed. Until April 1 an owner may return a different figure. If the assessors will not accept it, they send a notice, and the 45 days count from that date.

  • Choose the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator to hear it.
  • To keep going, give written notice that you want Superior Court.
  • The grounds that work are taxability, value and uniformity. Grumbling about the total tax does not qualify.

Skipping a return you were required to file costs 10 percent of whatever value you left off. The same site gives a mobile home owner 21 days to carry a corrected value to the equalization board. Where the owner is deployed, a friend or relative may file on their behalf, with 90 days from the value notice.

sections.h2: Which Screven County homestead and relief programs matter?
sections.html:
Owning and living in the house on January 1 is the test. File with the assessors, and get the form in before April 1 or it waits for the next year. A first-time owner brings the warranty deed. Approval carries forward on its own until you move, retitle or ask for another type.

Screven adds local exemptions of its own, and any local amount larger than the state one replaces it. A further exemption opens at age 62. Separately, the state deferral program lets a homeowner of 62 or more with gross income no higher than $15,000 postpone the tax, with the balance coming due at a transfer or once it hits 85 percent of market value.

Bona fide farm tracts are assessed at 30 percent in place of 40, and conservation tracts at current use value. A ten year covenant with the assessors comes with either.

sections.h2: How are mobile homes taxed in Screven County?
sections.html:
A mobile home is personal property in the commissioner's eyes. One sitting in Screven on New Year's Day owes tax by April 1, must be registered with the assessors, needs a location permit and has to show a decal. Neglect can bring a 10 percent penalty, a Magistrate Court summons or a sale of the unit.

Those bills typically mail around January 2. The state sheet gives a newly placed home 30 days to get its permit.

sections.h2: What should I gather before listing a Screven County house?
sections.html:
A little preparation saves a second trip to Sylvania. Every item below comes from an office listed above.

  • A written balance from the Tax Commissioner for every tax year still open, with the interest to date.
  • A copy of the warranty deed from the Clerk of Superior Court, if the family no longer holds the original.
  • Your latest assessment notice from the Tax Assessors, so the buyer sees the value the county uses.
  • Proof of homestead status, or a note that none was ever filed.
  • For a mobile home, the location permit and decal record.

If the owner has died, the person handling the estate should bring the same papers plus whatever court order gives authority to sign. Ask the commissioner's counter what proof it needs before it will discuss the account.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Screven County house that has unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Yes. Your closing attorney asks the commissioner for a payoff, and the closer pays it from what you receive at the table. A recorded fi. fa. must be released so the buyer can take clean title.

Cash buyers suit inherited, empty or worn houses, since no lender inspection stands in the way. Set any offer beside a listing price less repairs and a slower close.

faqs.q: Does Screven County want its tax in November or December?
faqs.a: Both dates appear on the commissioner's site, November 15 on the FAQ and December 20 on the general information page. Your bill's printed date rules, and 912-564-2206 can confirm it.

faqs.q: Where does a Screven homeowner file for homestead?
faqs.a: At the Tax Assessors' office, 912-564-7918. Forms that arrive by April 1 count for that year.

faqs.q: How soon must a Screven value dispute be filed?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date. The assessors hear it first, and then the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: What does a Screven mobile home owner pay each spring?
faqs.a: The tax and the location permit both come due April 1, and a missed date brings a 10 percent penalty.

faqs.q: Can an older Screven owner postpone the tax?
faqs.a: Yes, at age 62 or more with gross household income of $15,000 or less. The postponed amount stays owed and comes due at a transfer or when it reaches 85 percent of market value.
